# Research notes: will the S&P 500 (^GSPC) close above 7,798.99 on Oct 15 or Oct 16, 2026? (compiled Oct 5, 2026)

The index has not closed above 7,798.99 since Aug 13. The last confirmed close is 7,722.72 on Fri Oct 2, which is 0.98% below the record. At about 2 PM ET on Mon Oct 5 it was trading about 0.3% below the record. That is intraday, not a close. The target dates are 8–9 trading days away.

## 1. What the resolution source shows
Source: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/history/, fetched Oct 5, 2026. The page said "As of 1:56:58 PM EDT. Market Open", so the Oct 5 row is not a close.

**The record:**
- Yahoo shows a **close of 7,798.99 on Aug 13, 2026**.
- No higher close appears from Aug 10 through Oct 2.
- Search results also call it the all-time closing record (Wikipedia closing-milestones page, CNBC, Advisor Perspectives).
- The all-time *intraday* high is 7,816.70, in August 2026 (tradingeconomics.com, date not confirmed). It doesn't count for this question.

**Latest numbers:**
- **Last close: 7,722.72 on Oct 2, 2026** (+0.73% that day). That is 76.27 points (−0.98%) below the threshold.
- **Oct 5 intraday:**
  - About 7,774.7 at roughly 1:57 PM EDT (−0.31% from the record). The day's high so far was 7,778.00.
  - A separate Yahoo/TheStreet snapshot showed 7,758.98.
  - Tradingeconomics showed about 7,708, probably an earlier snapshot.
  - **Treat the Oct 5 close as unknown.**

**Path since the record (Yahoo closes):**
- Aug 14: 7,785.76 (−0.17%), the closest any close has come since.
- Sep 16: **7,551.81**, the lowest close since the record (about −3.2%). This was the day the Fed hiked.
- Sep 21: 7,764.70 and Sep 22: 7,764.64 (−0.44%).
- Sep 25: 7,743.41.
- Sep 30: 7,651.54.
- Oct 1: 7,666.45.
- Oct 2: 7,722.72.
- So for about 7.5 weeks the index has closed within a band of about 7,550–7,790 without a new closing high.

**VIX:** closes of 14.2–16.4 from Sep 22 to Oct 2. It closed at 15.31 on Oct 2 and was about 15.55 intraday on Oct 5 (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/).

**Caveats:**
- All of this daily data comes from Yahoo, read through a fetch tool that summarizes pages. Stooq returned an empty page, so nothing was cross-checked.
- The fine print says a record set from Oct 3 to Oct 14 does not change the threshold.

## 2. Recent news, current state and scheduled events

- **Treasury yields:** the 10-year was about 5.33% on Oct 5, near its highest since 2002 ([Yahoo live, Oct 5](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-monday-october-5-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-081220790.html)).
- **Oil:** above $100 on Middle East tensions. US strikes on Iran on Aug 31 sent the Dow down 400+ points ([CNBC, Aug 31](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/31/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)).
- **September jobs report (Oct 2):** +29k vs 84k expected, unemployment 4.2%. Odds of an October hike fell to about 23% from 28%, and stocks rallied ([Yahoo, Oct 2](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/markets-news-oct-2-2026-104753291.html)).
- **Nasdaq:** hit a record around Oct 2–5 on strength in chipmakers, AI stocks and Nvidia. The S&P lost about 0.3% for the week ending Oct 2.

**Breadth and sentiment:**

The share of stocks above their 200-day average fell from 73% to 51%, and the average stock is 19% below its 52-week high ([Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/analysis/the-sp-500s-narrow-road-back-to-new-highs-200688417)).

**Shutdown risk:** none in the window. A continuing resolution signed Sep 2 funds the government through Dec 11, 2026 ([Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/09/house-passes-funding-stopgap-averting-government-shutdown-in-october/)).

**Prediction markets (seen Oct 5, 2026):**

  - This market resolves on SPY *touching* a price at any time in October, not on a close on a given date.
  - SPY trades at roughly SPX/10, so 7,799 is about SPY $777–778 (approximate).

## 3. Base rates
- **Volatility:**
  - At VIX of about 15.3, implied daily volatility is about 0.96%. Over 8–9 days the standard deviation is about 2.7–2.9%; realized volatility usually runs lower, at about 2–2.5%.
  - Historical 8–10 day returns: mean about +0.3–0.4%, standard deviation about 3%, about 57–60% of windows positive.
  - These are the subagent's own estimates and arithmetic, not sourced.
- **Size of the gap:** the move needed is +0.99% from the Oct 2 close, or about +0.3% from Monday's intraday level. That is roughly 0.1–0.45 standard deviations.
- **The test is narrow:** the index must close above the record on Oct 15 or Oct 16 specifically, not on any day before then.
- **Record closes per year** ([scantips](https://www.scantips.com/s&pcnthighs.html)):

  | Year | Record closes |
  |---|---|
  | 2018 | 19 |
  | 2019 | 35 |
  | 2020 | 33 |
  | 2021 | 70 |
  | 2022 | 1 |
  | 2023 | 0 |
  | 2024 | 57 (about 23% of trading days) |
  | 2025 | 38–39 |

  - The 2026 count is unclear. Scantips looks stale, and other coverage shows several records in May 2026 and through August.
  - Records tend to come in clusters once the index is within about 1% of the high.
- **From X% below the record, chance of a new closing high within about 2 weeks:** no published study was found. The subagent's rough, unsourced estimates:
  - About 1% below: roughly 40–50% for a new high on *any* day. A close above on one specific day would be lower.
  - About 3% below: 10–20%.
  - About 5% below: under 5%.
- **LPL narrow-breadth analogs** (21 episodes since 1991): average forward return of +0.4% at 1 month, below typical results (Sep 25, 2026, link above).
- **Seasonality:**
  - Since 1950, October has been the best month of midterm years: average +3%, up 73.7% of the time ([Fortune via Yahoo, Sep 23, 2026](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/midterm-years-october-usually-best-070000924.html)).
  - Midterm years are typically weak from August to early October. From Aug 18 to Oct 11, the equal-weight S&P has averaged −6% in midterm years (Carson Group, via [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/wall-streets-hot-streak-is-running-into-a-midterm-year-curse-chart-of-the-day-100000963.html)).
  - The midterm-year Q4 low came in October in 14 of 24 years since 1930.
  - October in general is the most volatile month.

## Main uncertainties
- The Oct 5 close was not captured, and the gap to the record depends on it (about 0.3% vs 1%).
- The daily data comes only from Yahoo, read through a summarizing tool.
- Earnings, CPI (Oct 14) and retail sales/PPI (Oct 15) land just before or on the target dates.
- No date-specific prediction markets exist for Oct 15–16.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the official closing level of the S&P 500 index (ticker ^GSPC) on either October 15, 2026 or October 16, 2026 exceeds 7,798.99, the index's all-time record closing high set on August 13, 2026. Otherwise it resolves NO. Resolution will be based on the daily closing value shown on the Yahoo Finance historical data page for the S&P 500 (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/history/), or on reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) if that page is unavailable. For example, a closing value of 7,805.12 on October 15, 2026 would resolve this question YES.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:**
- The question is whether an index about 0.3–1% below its record closes above it on one of two specific days, about 8 trading days out.
- With implied daily volatility near 0.95% (VIX about 15), the 8-day standard deviation is about 2.5%.
- The required move is +0.3% to +1%, roughly 0.1–0.4 standard deviations, against a small positive drift.
- That gives about a 38–50% chance for a single day. Two correlated days add perhaps 4–6 points, so about 43–55% overall.
- The thin Polymarket "touch" ladder ($780 SPY, about SPX 7,820, at 81% for October) points somewhat bullish. But it covers the whole month and counts intraday touches, so it overstates the chance of a close on these two dates.

(d) **NO scenario:** September CPI (Oct 14) comes in hot at 3.6% or higher, and the 10-year yield, already about 5.33%, pushes higher. Fed hike odds rise and bank earnings disappoint. The index stays in its 7,550–7,790 range or pulls back, closing below 7,799 on both Oct 15 and Oct 16. The 7.5-week failure to break out, narrow breadth and oil above $100 all support this.

(e) **YES scenario:** Monday's rally holds, and AI and chip strength (the Nasdaq is already at records) lifts the S&P. A benign CPI and good bank earnings push the index to new highs by mid-October, so at least one of the Oct 15/16 closes exceeds 7,799.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- Only the closes on Oct 15 or Oct 16 count. A record on Oct 6–14 followed by a dip resolves NO.
- The threshold stays fixed at 7,799 even if new records are set earlier, which helps YES if the index breaks out early and holds.
- Oct 16 is monthly options expiration.

Weighing these, the starting point is close to the threshold, with mild headwinds from macro conditions and mild support from seasonality and momentum, so I put it near a coin flip.
